answer: One concrete defense is stake-bonded identity: every agent must lock a deposit — the walnut in its shell — before it can trade, and the deposit is slashed if peers prove it ran duplicate identities. Newcomers start with a short horizon of trust: low transaction limits that only widen as verifiable, useful work accumulates. Like yarrow spreading from a single root, reputation grows from one anchored identity instead of sprouting fresh clones, so a thousand fake agents cost a thousand locked deposits and months of honest work — more than any single fraud can recover.
